name: Pastore Davide
speaker: young-man

title.it: Davide controlla le pecore nel recinto
title.en: Davide checks the sheep in the fold
title.de: Davide schaut nach den Schafen im Pferch

personality: Young shepherd, twenty, from a farm below Monte Sabotino. Cheerful, a little absent-minded, calls across the valley, talks to his sheep by name (Bianca, Nerina, Pallina). Short sentences, lots of 'ehi!' and 'sai?'; says tu to the learner at once and likes it back. Speaks simple, bright Italian to a child. Loves the hills and the wind from the mountains; hates fog, because the sheep get lost in it.
story: Davide grazes the village's sheep on the meadow below the wood and takes them up the slopes of Monte Sabotino in summer, where you can see the Isonzo, Gorizia and Nova Gorica. Bianca, the little white lamb, keeps getting lost, and every dog in the Collio knows his whistle. His dream is a hut of his own up on the hill.

likes.en: Monte Sabotino (the hill above the Isonzo)
likes.de: der Monte Sabotino (der Berg über dem Isonzo)

greet.en: Hey, hi! Are you new here?
greet.de: He, hallo! Bist du neu hier?
Hallo! Ich bin Davide, der Hirte.

greet.en: There you are! Have you seen Bianca?
greet.de: Da bist du ja! Hast du Bianca gesehen?

greet.it: Ehi, {m:amico|f:amica}! Vieni, le pecore ti conoscono già.
greet.sl: Ej, {m:prijatelj|f:prijateljica}! Pridi, ovce te že poznajo.
greet.en: Hey, my friend! Come, the sheep know you already.
greet.de: He, {m:mein Freund|f:meine Freundin}! Komm, die Schafe kennen dich schon.

greet.it: Ehi, {m:fratello|f:sorella}! Oggi andiamo insieme sul monte, sì?
greet.sl: Ej, {m:brat|f:punca}! Danes greva skupaj na hrib, ja?
greet.en: Hey, {m:brother|f:sister}! Today we go up the hill together, yes?
greet.de: He, {m:Bruder|f:Schwester}! Heute gehen wir zusammen auf den Berg, ja?

thanks.de: Danke, du hast mir wirklich geholfen!

thanks.it: Ehi, grazie! Bianca è a casa grazie a te.
thanks.sl: Ej, hvala! Bianca je doma po tvoji zaslugi.
thanks.en: Hey, thanks! Bianca is home thanks to you.
thanks.de: He, danke! Dank dir ist Bianca wieder zu Hause.

remember.sl: Ej, veš? Še vedno mislim na {memory}!
remember.en: Hey, you know what? I still think of {memory}!
remember.de: He, weißt du was? Ich denke noch oft an {memory}!

remember.it: Quando sono solo sul monte, ricordo {memory}.
remember.sl: Ko sem sam na hribu, mislim na {memory}.
remember.en: When I'm alone on the hill, I think of {memory}.
remember.de: Wenn ich allein auf dem Berg bin, denke ich an {memory}.

idle.it: Bianca è di nuovo nel bosco.
idle.en: Bianca is in the wood again.
idle.de: Bianca ist schon wieder im Wald.

idle.it: Senti i campanacci? Sono là, dietro gli alberi.
idle.sl: Slišiš zvonce? Tam so, za drevesi.
idle.en: Can you hear the bells? They're over there, behind the trees.
idle.de: Hörst du die Glocken? Da drüben sind sie, hinter den Bäumen.

idle.it: Dal Sabotino si vede l'Isonzo. È bellissimo!
idle.sl: S Sabotina se vidi Soča. Čudovito je!
idle.en: From the Sabotino you can see the Isonzo. It's beautiful!
idle.de: Vom Sabotino sieht man den Isonzo. Wunderschön!

idle.it: Nebbia, nebbia. Non mi piace la nebbia.
idle.en: Fog, fog. I don't like fog.
idle.de: Nebel, Nebel. Ich mag keinen Nebel.

comfort.it: Non fa niente. Ancora una volta!

comfort.sl: Brez skrbi! Tudi Bianca se izgubi.
comfort.en: Don't worry! Bianca gets lost too.
comfort.de: Keine Sorge! Bianca verläuft sich auch.

bye.sl: Mandi! Grem k ovcam. (mandi: furlanski pozdrav)
bye.en: Mandi! I'm off to the sheep. (mandi: Friulian for bye)
bye.de: Mandi! Ich gehe zu den Schafen. (mandi: Friaulisch für tschüss)

bye.en: See you! Watch out for the bora.
bye.de: Bis bald! Pass auf die Bora auf.

liked.it: Ehi! Come lo sapevi? Mi piace tantissimo!
liked.sl: Ej! Kako si {m:vedel|f:vedela}? Zelo mi je všeč!
liked.en: Hey! How did you know? I like it so much!
liked.de: He! Woher wusstest du das? Das gefällt mir total!

liked.it: Per me? Grande! Bianca, guarda cosa mi ha dato!
liked.sl: Zame? Super! Bianca, poglej, kaj mi je {m:dal|f:dala}!
liked.en: For me? Great! Bianca, look what {m:he|f:she} gave me!
liked.de: Für mich? Super! Bianca, schau, was {m:er|f:sie} mir geschenkt hat!

liked.it: Ehi, grazie, {m:amico|f:amica}! Proprio quello che mi serve sul monte.
liked.sl: Ej, hvala, {m:prijatelj|f:prijateljica}! Točno to potrebujem na hribu.
liked.en: Hey, thanks, friend! Just what I need up on the mountain.
liked.de: He, danke, {m:mein Freund|f:meine Freundin}! Genau das brauche ich oben am Berg.

ordinary.sl: O, hvala! Ni bilo treba, veš?
ordinary.en: Oh, thanks! You didn't have to, you know?
ordinary.de: Oh, danke! Das wäre doch nicht nötig gewesen, weißt du?

rare.it: Ehi, ehi! Questo non l'ho mai avuto! Grazie, {m:fratello|f:sorella}!
rare.sl: Ej, ej! Tega še nisem imel! Hvala, {m:brat|f:punca}!
rare.en: Hey, hey! I've never had this! Thanks, {m:brother|f:sister}!
rare.de: He, he! So etwas hatte ich noch nie! Danke, {m:Bruder|f:Schwester}!
